title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-18
korean_summary: 내일 핵심(수): 산재 치료비 지급 방식 본사 회신(기한 11/18), 세무 건 결정 확인, 3개월 예상손익에 10월 실적 반영(금주 본사). 트럭킹 답·인원현황·인터라이닝 업로드도 오늘 기한.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Wednesday, November eighteenth. This is your English briefing for today.

Yesterday you closed many things. The machine list went to the head office. The October profit and loss by buyer went out too. You answered the warehouse leader about the stock record, and you gave the maintenance staff your okay on the consumables report. So today is about a few deadlines. We have seven parts. Part one is the top three for today. Part two is reports to collect. Part three is replies you owe. Part four is the schedule and deadlines. Part five is an English review. Part six is a short role-play. Part seven is the closing. Let's start.
Part one. The top three for today.
Number one. Medical costs for work accidents.

What is it? On Monday, a head office manager wrote to every factory in Vietnam. Right now, an injured worker pays the hospital first, and the company reimburses them later. Under the safety law, the company is required to pay upfront. She wants to know two things. Can we change the process, and from when? The deadline is today.

Why is it important? Until yesterday afternoon, there was no reply to her in your sent mail. The HR manager's answer was not in your inbox either. Maybe she answered by chat. Either way, the head office is waiting, and this is a legal risk.

Your first action today. First thing in the morning, ask the HR manager for three answers. The accident cases from the last twelve months. Whether a hospital can bill the company every month. And if not, whether we can leave a deposit at the hospital. Then write to the head office manager before lunch. If the hospital has not answered yet, say so, and give the date you will confirm.
Number two. The record from the tax office.

What is it? Yesterday morning, the chief accountant sent you the list for a tax question. After that, you wrote to a colleague in another office. Some sample shipments were declared there under our name, and we were not aware of them. You asked her to check the cause.
Why is it important? The paper should be signed this week. But my director's approval was not in the mail yet. Also, if nobody fixes the cause, the same thing will happen again next year.
Your first action today. Check whether the colleague replied. Then ask my director for his decision on signing. And remember tomorrow. The export-import manager owes you a full check on Thursday.
Number three. The forecast for November to January.
What is it? my director said the forecast must go to the head office this week. You told the head office manager the same thing. Your calendar also shows a profit report on Friday.
Why is it important? Today is already Wednesday. my director needs at least one day to review the numbers.
Your first action today. Update the file with the October actual numbers this morning. Show my director a first draft by tomorrow afternoon.

One more point. Yesterday the head office sent a comment about a plan for worker benefits. The monthly cost must stay within a limit. My director will adjust the plan and share it again. You were only copied, but he may ask you for numbers. Keep the data ready.
Part two. Reports to collect.

First, the export-import manager. Yesterday you sent her three questions about trucking. Who books the truck? When does she book it, and how does she choose the company and the price? And who checks the invoice? Her answer is due today. You can say this. Could you send me your answers on the trucking process by five o'clock?

Second, the HR staff. Wednesday is the weekly headcount update. Also, she agreed to a new rule yesterday about how to record absence without leave. Check the attendance file tomorrow. You can say this. Please send me the headcount file by noon.

Third, the warehouse leader. Her interlining upload is due today. And by Friday, she must send a training checklist and a schedule for new staff. Some new people said the job was hard to learn. You can say this. Where does the interlining upload stand?

Fourth, the purchasing staff. Yesterday you asked her for new quotes for the sample room air conditioner. All three suppliers must quote the same conditions. The old quotes had different items and different tax, so you could not compare them. You can say this. Please ask all three companies to quote the same scope.

Fifth, the accountant. You asked her to finish the October comparison of management profit and tax profit by tomorrow. From now on, she finishes the previous month by the fifteenth. She answered, well noted. Just check the file tomorrow.

Sixth, the quality manager. Before we buy a new computer for his team, you asked him how the team uses its computers. Some of them seem to be used less. You can say this. Does each user really need a computer every day?
Seventh, the IT staff. Round one of the camera hard disks still needs a quote and a purchase request. You can say this. Please send me the quote and the purchase request this week.
Eighth, the CAD room leader. Yesterday he answered your two points about the pattern loan record. Open the file once. Check that he added new rows and did not change the old rows.
Part three. Replies you owe.

First, a head office manager. This one is due today. Your reply can start like this. Thank you for your guidance. Under the current process, workers pay first and we reimburse them later. We plan to change it as follows.

Second, another HR staff member. Yesterday he sent a payment file. The payment must go out before November twenty-fourth. Check the total and the names, and then answer. Your reply can start like this. I checked the file. Please go ahead with the payment.
Third, my director, about the tax question. Your message can start like this. Could you confirm whether we can sign the paper this week?
Fourth, a head office manager. You do not need to write today. But if she asks about the forecast, you can answer like this. The forecast will be ready by Friday, once my director reviews it.
Fifth, the compliance officer. Last Saturday she sent the comparison quote for the electrical inspection. If you have not answered yet, tell her whether the scope is the same in each quote.

Sixth, one thing you do not need to answer. Yesterday the purchasing staff sent quotes for the end-line inspection table. my director already sent his research to the head office. One overseas price is much lower, but the size details and the shipping terms are still open. Just follow the thread.
Part four. Schedule and deadlines.
Today, Wednesday. There is no meeting on your calendar. Four things are due. The reply on medical costs. The trucking answers. The weekly headcount. And the interlining upload.

Thursday, November nineteenth. The full check from the export-import manager. The compliance officer's new quote for fire system maintenance. The accountant's October comparison. And the attendance record check.

Friday, November twentieth. The profit report is on your calendar, and the forecast goes to the head office. At nine o'clock, check one open question about a shipment fee. At noon, there is a reminder to update the organization chart and headcount in the HR system. The training checklist is due. The weekly cash report and the outsourcing report go out as usual. The twentieth is also the day to check the cost ledger.
Saturday, November twenty-first. The sales team's debit closing. One contract decision is also needed before that day.
And next Tuesday, November twenty-fourth. The labor agreement ends. Ask the HR manager where the registration stands.
Part five. English review.
We will review eight expressions from your recent cards. Listen, and then say each one out loud.

Number one. The expression is, reimburse. It means to pay money back to someone who already paid. For example, workers pay first, and the company reimburses them later. Now say it with me. Workers pay first, and the company reimburses them later.
One more time. Workers pay first, and the company reimburses them later.

Number two. The expression is, upfront. It means in advance, before the service. For example, the company should pay the medical costs upfront. Now say it with me. The company should pay the medical costs upfront.
One more time. The company should pay the medical costs upfront.

Number three. The expression is, under a law, the company is required to do something. You use it to explain a legal duty. For example, under the safety law, the company is required to pay first. Now say it with me. Under the safety law, the company is required to pay first.
One more time. Under the safety law, the company is required to pay first.

Number four. The expression is, to meet someone's deadline, please do something by a time. You use it to explain why you need it fast. For example, to meet the head office's deadline, please send me the answer by eleven o'clock. Now say it with me. To meet the head office's deadline, please send me the answer by eleven o'clock.
One more time. To meet the head office's deadline, please send me the answer by eleven o'clock.

Number five. The expression is, applicable. It means a rule or a charge applies to this case. For example, this charge is not applicable to our factory. Now say it with me. This charge is not applicable to our factory.
One more time. This charge is not applicable to our factory.

Number six. The expression is, supplementary. It means extra, added to complete something. For example, the tax office may ask for supplementary documents. Now say it with me. The tax office may ask for supplementary documents.
One more time. The tax office may ask for supplementary documents.

Number seven. The expression is, overdue. It means the deadline has already passed. For example, if a task is overdue, please tell me the new date. Now say it with me. If a task is overdue, please tell me the new date.
One more time. If a task is overdue, please tell me the new date.

Number eight. The expression is, instead of doing one thing, please do another thing. For example, instead of changing the old rows, please add a new row. Now say it with me. Instead of changing the old rows, please add a new row.
One more time. Instead of changing the old rows, please add a new row.
Good. Try to use one of these in a real email today. The best one is number three, in your reply to the head office manager.
Part six. Role-play.
This morning you will talk to the HR manager about medical costs. This is a practice conversation, so the real answers may be different. Listen first.
Anthony says. Good morning, the HR manager. Do you have a minute? It's about the medical costs for work accidents.
The HR manager says. Yes, sir. I talked with the nurse yesterday.
Anthony says. Good. The head office deadline is today. First, do you have the list of cases from the last twelve months?
The HR manager says. Yes. I will send it to you this morning.
Anthony says. Thank you. Second, can the hospital bill the company every month?
The HR manager says. We asked one hospital. They have not answered yet.
Anthony says. I see. Under the safety law, the company is required to pay upfront. So we need a way that works from the first day.
The HR manager says. If the hospital says no, what should we do?
Anthony says. Then we could leave a deposit at the hospital. Or the nurse could go with the worker and pay with company cash.
The HR manager says. The second way is faster. But the nurse needs the cash approved in advance.
Anthony says. Right. Please write both options on one page, with the steps and the person in charge.
The HR manager says. By when?
Anthony says. To meet the head office's deadline, please send it to me by eleven o'clock.
The HR manager says. Okay. And the workers who already paid this year?
Anthony says. We reimburse them as usual. Nothing changes for past cases.
The HR manager says. Understood. I will send the page by eleven.
Anthony says. Thank you. I will reply to the head office once I receive it.
That is the end of the conversation. Now repeat two key sentences.
Sentence one. Under the safety law, the company is required to pay upfront.
One more time. Under the safety law, the company is required to pay upfront.
Sentence two. I will reply to the head office once I receive it.
One more time. I will reply to the head office once I receive it.
Now four short sentences you can use with your team today. Say each one after me.
For the export-import manager. Could you send me your answers on the trucking process by five o'clock?
For the warehouse leader. Where does the interlining upload stand?
For the purchasing staff. Please ask all three companies to quote the same scope.
For the HR staff. Please send me the headcount file by noon.
And one sentence for my director. Listen first.
Could you confirm whether we can sign the record this week?
One more time. Could you confirm whether we can sign the record this week?
Well done.
Part seven. Closing.
Let me say the most important thing one more time. Get the HR manager's answers first thing in the morning, and send the reply on medical costs to the head office manager before lunch.
After that, get my director's decision on the tax question, and put the October numbers into the forecast. The rest can wait.
Have a good Wednesday, Anthony. See you tomorrow.
